summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes, chronic back pain, and anxiety was admitted for recurrent nausea, vomiting, and hyperglycemia after eating contaminated food. Her blood glucose was 627 on admission but not in DKA. She improved with IV fluids, insulin, and antiemetics, and tolerated a regular diet without further vomiting. A gastric emptying study was normal, and blood cultures showed no infection. Her A1C was elevated at 12.8%, prompting adjustment of her insulin regimen to 28 units Lantus at bedtime and a revised carb-to-insulin ratio of 1:12 with correction scale of 1 unit Humalog per 40 points above 140. She expressed motivation to improve adherence and was connected with a new primary care provider, social work, and GI follow-up for esophageal varices and H. pylori eradication. She was discharged home in stable condition with updated medications and close outpatient support planned.
